paper_metadata.title: Semi-Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction by Relation Pattern Extraction
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper proposes a semi-automatic method for knowledge-graph construction by extracting relation patterns and finding new relations. Relation patterns are represented as tag sequences, pattern similarity is learned from existing relation instances using a Siamese network, and similarity plus clustering is used to extract new patterns and detect new relations. Experiments on large-scale web pages evaluate similarity learning and new-relation clustering.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses semi-automatic extraction of relation-object facts from enterprise web pages when the same relation has different textual representations, website templates vary across sources, and templates change over time. It aims to reduce the manual annotation burden while constructing a knowledge graph and discovering previously unseen relations.

methodology.description: The system parses webpages into DOM trees and represents each relation-object instance as two XPath-derived tag sequences containing the relation and object text. Tag tokens are embedded with a Skip-Gram word2vec model trained on DOM-parsing output. Concatenated embeddings are processed by two shared five-layer fully connected feature-map networks forming a Siamese architecture. The learned distance metric identifies similar instances, whose centroid forms a relation pattern. Seed patterns are iteratively expanded and refined with newly extracted instances; clustering of instances is additionally used to detect patterns for new relations.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: No external ontology is reported. Existing relation names and manually supplied seed relation instances define the initial relation schema; newly discovered relation clusters are not automatically assigned semantic labels.

evidence.excerpt: Given some instances of the relations for an entity, the system build the relation patterns and find more relation instances from web pages.
The future work includes finding new representation of the relation patterns and give the labels for new relations automatically.

input_output.input_type: Enterprise-company webpages containing semi-structured textual fields and DOM structure
input_output.input_granularity: Webpage-level relation-object instances, represented by XPath/DOM tag sequences for the relation and its object
input_output.output_representation: Knowledge-graph triples for company entities and relations; intermediate outputs are relation extraction patterns, similarity scores, and clusters for existing or new relations

datasets: Enterprise Knowledge Graph dataset: Japanese company websites; 2,717,653 company entities and 22,257,276 triples
Ten-relation similarity-learning subset with 286,276 instances: name, address, person, homepage, phone number, rel-org, finance, size, date, and product
Unseen relation dataset: fax, email, permission, introduction, domains, and offices

evaluation.setting: Similarity learning is trained and evaluated on labeled genuine/impostor pairs from ten known relations, with experiments varying the number of instances and iteration steps. Generalization is tested on unseen relations separated from training, using a validation set to select the threshold and a test set to calculate FA, FR, and EER. New-relation detection is evaluated by clustering test data into the known number of categories and comparing assigned cluster labels with true labels using precision and recall.

value: On the ten known relations, using 10,000 instances and 100 iteration steps produced EER 0.04; using 10,000 instances and 500 iteration steps produced EER 0.01.
On the unseen-relation dataset, the system achieved EER 0.05.

For clustering-based new-relation detection, K-Means generally outperformed hierarchical clustering in the reported precision/recall results. K-Means precision/recall included fax 0.7284/0.912, email 0.9134/0.770, permission 0.7414/0.671, introduction 0.9989/0.882, domains 0.8503/1.00, and offices 0.9883/0.93.
The authors report that performance improves as the number of instances per relation increases and tends toward convergence at approximately 1,000 instances per relation.

value: (Author claim) The approach reduces dependence on exhaustive manual annotations by starting from a small set of labeled relation instances and expanding patterns iteratively.
(Experimental result) The learned similarity metric supports transfer from known relations to unseen relations, with reported unseen-data EER of 0.05.
(Review-level inference) Representing relation instances through DOM/XPath tag sequences directly addresses cross-template layout variation, although the method remains tied to webpage structure.
(Experimental result) The method supports both extraction of more instances for existing relations and clustering-based discovery of new relation groups.

value: (Review-level inference) The input setting is semi-structured enterprise webpages rather than ordinary free text, so applicability to prose is not demonstrated.
(Review-level inference) The method requires manually labeled seed instances and pair labels for similarity learning, leaving a nontrivial annotation requirement.
(Author-reported future work) New relations are not automatically assigned semantic labels.
(Review-level inference) The clustering evaluation prespecifies the number of categories and requires cluster-label assignment, which may not reflect open-world deployment.
(Review-level inference) The reported experiments do not include comparisons with an experimental baseline.
